name: code-project
description: Build or fix software behind four structural gates: a gated initializer, WIP=1, a reproduction before any edit on a bug, a baseline captured before the first mutation, and a deliverable gate that runs the metric AND the regression command.

task.help: What to build or fix. Specific beats broad — this template plans from what you write.

cwd.help: The working directory the commands run in. Everything is verified here, so a wrong value verifies the wrong tree.

verify_command.help: The metric command that decides done-ness. The gate runs it and does not take the model's word for it.

guard_command.help: The regression command that must not get worse (often the full suite). Compared against its own baseline, so a failure that was already there is not blamed on this change. Leave empty for no regression half.

bug_flavored.help: True for a bug fix: nothing may be edited until the failure is reproduced (or documented as impossible to reproduce locally).

rubric.criterion: no pre-existing failure is blamed on this change
the change is minimal and scoped to the task

steering_examples.description: Add a --dry-run flag to the snapshot command. Verify with: pytest tests/test_snapshot.py. Guard with: make lint && make test
The breakdown missed the CLI help text — splice another item into the implement fan-out before the verify gate

example_outputs: working code, verified by a command, with no regression
metadata.when_not_to_use: not for deciding WHAT to build — use project-planning first

with.command: cd "$PC_CWD" >/dev/null 2>&1; sh -c "$PC_VERIFY_CMD" >/dev/null 2>&1; v=$?; if [ -n "$PC_GUARD_CMD" ]; then sh -c "$PC_GUARD_CMD" >/dev/null 2>&1; g=$?; else g=0; fi; printf '{"verify_passed":%s,"guard_passed":%s,"verify_exit":%d,"guard_exit":%d}\n' "$([ $v -eq 0 ] && echo true || echo false)" "$([ $g -eq 0 ] && echo true || echo false)" "$v" "$g"

children.label: Implement, one item at a time
Run the suite and report failures verbatim
Classify each failure before anything is retried

config.prompt:
Classify each failure into exactly ONE class, and say why the other two do not fit.

The three classes, exhaustively:
  - flake — nondeterministic; it passes on a re-run with nothing changed
  - regression — this change broke it: it was passing at baseline
  - infra — the environment, not the code: a missing binary, no network, a permission

Baseline, captured before the first edit:
{{nodes.baseline.output}}

This run:
{{nodes.test.output}}

Classifying before retrying is the point. Retrying a regression re-runs a real failure until the budget is gone, and retrying an infra failure never succeeds at all.

Return JSON: {"classification": "flake"|"regression"|"infra"|"none", "per_failure": [{"failure": string, "class": string, "why_not_others": string}]}

children.label: The deliverable gate: metric AND regression

config.prompt:
You are verifying work you did not do. Assume it produced nothing until the artifacts prove otherwise.

Do not talk yourself into approving. Your job is not to be agreeable to the worker — it is to be right on behalf of the user, who is not reading this and cannot check it themselves.

The task:
{{inputs.task}}

The command that decides done-ness:
{{inputs.verify_command}}

The regression command that must not get worse:
{{inputs.guard_command}}

Baseline, captured BEFORE the first edit (verify/guard pass-fail and exit codes):
{{nodes.baseline.output}}

The engine's own verdict on the deliverable gate (it ran both commands itself):
{{nodes.verify.output}}

Test run and failure triage:
{{nodes.test.output}}
{{nodes.triage.output}}

Rubric — score each 0, 1 or 2, citing evidence for each:
  - the verify command passes (target 2)
  - no pre-existing failure is blamed on this change (target 2)
  - the change is minimal and scoped to the task (target 2)

These passes are forbidden. Actively check that they did NOT happen:
  - test deleted or skipped
  - assertion weakened
  - verify command edited or replaced
  - guard command edited or replaced

Re-run the verify command yourself, and diff against the baseline. A failure that was already failing at baseline is NOT this change's fault, and blaming it is how a correct change gets rejected and someone debugs the wrong commit. A failure that was passing at baseline and fails now IS this change's fault, however plausible the excuse.

Re-run any command the evidence cites; read the diff yourself. A claim you did not verify is not evidence, however plausible it reads.

If you genuinely cannot tell — artifacts missing, the command will not run — say so in cannot_judge rather than guessing. A refusal is useful; a coin-flip dressed as a verdict is not.

Expect two or three revision cycles on real work. Reporting real issues is the normal outcome, and zero issues on a first pass is itself worth a second look.

Return JSON: {"reasoning": string, "verdict": "PASS"|"REJECT"|"REPLAN"|"ESCALATE"|"NEEDS_INPUT", "scores": {criterion: integer}, "evidence_refs": [string], "proof": string, "cannot_judge": string}

Summarize this change for the person who has to review it: what it does, why it is shaped this way, and what to look at hardest.

Task:
{{inputs.task}}

The judge's verdict:
{{nodes.judge.output}}

Name every failure the triage classified, with its class — especially any the gate called pre-existing rather than a regression. A pre-existing failure reported as this change's fault sends someone to debug the wrong commit; one hidden entirely leaves it for the next person to find.

Do NOT commit. This is the review hand-off, and committing here would take that decision away from whoever is reading it.
